subject.title: fix(promotions): guard JSON.parse against corrupt DB data

question: Should malformed persisted promotion notification data continue to use the existing whole-state `EMPTY_STATE` fallback, or should OpenClaw adopt a new per-row empty-history recovery behavior?
rationale: The patch changes the persistence-recovery boundary rather than only preventing an exception, and the two paths have different notification replay and recovery semantics.

options.title: Retain whole-state fallback
options.body: Let malformed row JSON reach the existing metadata-level fallback, then add a focused regression test and real persisted-state proof.

options.title: Adopt row-level recovery
options.body: Keep the leaf catch only with an explicit contract for duplicate-notification handling, tests, and a documented reason that row-level empty history is safe.

recommendation.title: Retain whole-state fallback
recommendation.body: Let malformed row JSON reach the existing metadata-level fallback, then add a focused regression test and real persisted-state proof.

likelyOwner.reason: File-history ownership was not established from the available review context, so the code-area owner should make the persistence-recovery choice.
